mutant.description: THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM is a pair of ABSENCES -- no forcing reaches the classifier, and no disclosure field exists -- and an absence is the claim most easily manufactured by a broken probe. So every absence is printed beside POSITIVE CONTROLS on the same instrument and the same bytes: the disclosure census prints 5 controls (generated_at, fixture_remove, verdict, unresolved, per_partner) alongside the 10 zeros, and the forcing census prints the --fixture-remove flag and its 3 applier sites -- i.e. it PROVES THE MECHANISM EXISTS while proving it is unreachable.

Forcing: the flag present (1) and its applier present (3) in the very file whose command line lacks it. AND THE CONTROL CAUGHT TWO OF MY OWN PROBES: a bare substring count of 'ses' returned 12 in a renderer with 0 SES call sites (uses/series/closes) -- a number that CONTRADICTED the claim it was printed to support -- and a doc-phrase probe with an embedded newline returned 0 and read as an absent guarantee where the guarantee is present. Both were corrected before this record and both now print the artifact value beside the real one.
